verdict.rationale: Nitrokey documents its own 'Touch Confirmation (Nitrokey 3 only)' feature for OpenPGP card operations, and lists FIDO2 SSH keys. Requiring a physical touch for sensitive cryptographic operations is the core mechanism of this story. The evidence is only a section heading, though, and nothing shows it being used to gate automated or agent-initiated actions. missing for 10: details on which operations can require touch and how it is configured, any documented use as an approval gate for agent or automated workflows (e.g. agent git signing or SSH), touch support across other applets and models, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can require a physical key touch as the human-approval step for sensitive automated or agent-initiated actions
